nodes.name: Peroxomolybdate preparation
nodes.procedure: 500 mg of Mo powder was taken in a 20 mL glass vial to which 6 mL of 30% w/w hydrogen peroxide was added dropwise, leading to an exothermic reaction forming a yellow colored peroxomolybdic solution.
nodes.source_text: 500 mg of Mo powder was taken in a 20 mL glass vial to which 6 mL of 30% w/w hydrogen peroxide was added dropwise...

nodes.name: HMTA solution preparation
nodes.procedure: 350 mg of hexamethylenetetramine (HMTA) (nitrogen source) was added to 10 mL deionized (DI) water and mixed well to obtain a transparent solution.
nodes.source_text: 350 mg of hexamethylenetetramine (HMTA) (nitrogen source) was added to 10 mL deionized (DI) water...

nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis with annealing
nodes.procedure: 320 mg of Ni foam was added to the peroxomolybdic solution along with the slow addition of the HMTA solution under continuous stirring for 30 min. The solution was transferred to a Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave, and a hydrothermal reaction was carried out at a temperature of 200°C for 24 h, then cooled naturally to room temperature. The sample was washed twice with DI water and ethanol, and the resulting powder sample was dried overnight in a vacuum oven at 40°C. The dried sample was then annealed in a tube furnace under continuous nitrogen flow at a temperature of 350°C for 2 h at the heating rate of 3°C min⁻¹.

nodes.name: Phosphorization
nodes.procedure: The annealed sample was phosphorized at 400°C with a heating rate of 3°C min⁻¹ under a nitrogen atmosphere for 3 h. Sodium hypophosphite was used as the phosphorus source while keeping the ratio between the sample and the P source at 1:30.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows ultrathin N-NiMoO₃ and N-NiMo₃P sheets with large lateral dimensions up to several microns and homogeneously distributed pores.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM images in Figure 1 show detailed morphological features and the texture of annealed N-NiMoO₃ and N-NiMo₃P sheets, where it is obvious that both samples possess ultrathin features and large lateral dimensions up to several microns.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice spacing of 0.378 nm for (110) plane of MoO₃ in N-NiMo₃ and 0.239 nm for (002) plane of Mo₃P in N-NiMo₃P, confirming successful conversion to phosphide with defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lattice spacing of 0.378 nm for N-NiMo₃ corresponds to the (110) plane of MoO₃ according to JCPDS No. 35-0609 ... and 0.239 nm for N-NiMo₃P corresponds to the (002) plane of Mo₃P according to JCPDS No. 89-2587.

properties.description: High-resolution image showing thin, straight, elongated nanostructures with uniform width, resembling nanowires or nanofibers. Gray background with white contrast, scale bar 100 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM confirms ultrathin sheets with thicknesses of 3.3 nm for N-NiMoO₃ and 3.2 nm for N-NiMo₃P with evidence of pores.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The thickness of oxide and phosphide sheets calculated using topological images are 3.3 nm ... and 3.2 nm, respectively.

Upon phosphorization, new peaks emerge at 26°, 37°, 41.5°, 44°, 49.5°, 53.5°, 60.5°, and 66.6°, corresponding to the crystal planes (220), (002), (202), (222), (431), (402), (611), and (442) of Mo₃P, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows N-NiMoO₃ peaks at 243, 288, 342, 373, and 820 cm⁻¹ ascribed to α-MoO₃ with 4 cm⁻¹ shift due to defects; no peaks for N-NiMo₃P confirming phosphide conversion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: N-NiMoO₃ shows peaks at 243, 288, 342, 373, and 820 cm⁻¹ ascribed to α-MoO₃. ... Interestingly, no peaks were recorded for N-NiMo₃P, confirming the successful conversion of oxide into phosphide.

nodes.characterization_summary: FIR-FTIR shows N-NiMoO₃ metal-oxygen peaks at 432, 594, ≈252, 262, 368 cm⁻¹ disappearing after phosphorization; N-NiMo₃P shows new peaks at ≈400, ≈1038 cm⁻¹ (phosphate), broader peaks at ≈1278, ≈1634 cm⁻¹ (phosphate/nitrate, hydroxyl).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The N-NiMoO₃ sample shows strong peaks of 432 and 594 cm⁻¹ in the spectral range of 400-650 cm⁻¹ and further peaks at ≈252, 262, and 368 cm⁻¹ are attributed to metal-oxygen bonds. ... new peaks at ≈400 and ≈1038 cm⁻¹ appear in the case of N-NiMo₃P, attributing to the phosphate ion along with broader peaks at ≈1278 and ≈1634 cm⁻¹, indicating the presence of phosphate/nitrate and hydroxyl groups, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: BET surface areas are 3.99 m²g⁻¹ for oxide and 19.29 m²g⁻¹ for phosphide; pore volume increases from 1.28×10⁻³ to 5.10×10⁻³ cm³g⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Applying Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) analysis, the surface areas for the oxide and phosphide were calculated to be 3.99 and 19.29 m²g⁻¹, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Mo 3d peaks at 235.2/232.1 eV (Mo⁶⁺/Mo⁴⁺) in oxide, new 230.2 eV (Mo-P) in phosphide; Ni 2p shifts by 1 eV; N 1s at 397.8 eV (M-N); P 2p at 130.56/133.9 eV (M-P/PO₄³⁻).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3a presents the Mo 3d deconvoluted spectra of both oxide and phosphide, showing two major peaks around 235.2 and 232.1 eV could be attributed to 3d₃/₂(Mo⁶⁺) and 3d₃/₂(Mo⁴⁺), respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM-EDS shows uniform distribution of N, Ni, Mo, O in N-NiMoO₃ and N, Ni, Mo, P in N-NiMo₃P across sheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To observe the distribution of elements across the different sheets, energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) elemental maps were recorded. These indicate the uniform distribution of N, Ni, Mo, and O throughout N-NiMoO₃.
